pass_a_gloss: If as the sufferings of Christ overflow, so through Christ overflows also the comfort, let us most readily accept the sufferings of Christ, and let it overflow in us, if indeed we reach out for abundant comfort, with which all the mourning ones will be comforted, but perhaps not on equal terms. For if on equal terms the comfort were, there would not have been written the word: as the sufferings of Christ overflow into us, so overflows also our comfort. The partners of the sufferings, according to the proportion of the sufferings of which they are partners toward Christ, will be partners also of the comfort; which things you also learn from the one saying such things as one entrusted: for we know that as you are partners of the sufferings, so also of the comfort. And God says through a prophet: in a received season I gave ear to you and in a day of salvation I ran to help you. What other well-received season then, than when, because of the reverence toward God in Christ, under guard, going in procession in the world and leading a triumph rather than being led in triumph, we are led off? For the witnesses in Christ together with him strip off the rulers and the authorities and celebrate triumph together with him, as becoming partners of his sufferings, so also of the brave exploits in his sufferings; from which is also the triumphing over the rulers and the authorities, which after a little you will see beaten and disgraced. What other day so of salvation as the day of such a deliverance of ours from here? But I exhort: give no cause of stumbling in nothing, so that the body of elders or the service may not be found fault with by you, but in all set yourselves forth as servants of God, in much endurance, saying: and now what is my endurance? not the Lord? in tribulations, being convinced that many are the tribulations of the just; in compulsions, so that we may demand the blessedness as necessary to us; in tight places, so that, having journeyed without leaving anything out the tight and pressed road as it were, we may reach to the life. If it is needful, let us set ourselves forth also in strokes and in guard-houses and in unsettlements and in toils and in wakefulness and in fasts. For see the Lord, and his wage in hand, to give back to each as his works are.
pass_b_english: If “as the sufferings of Christ abound, so through Christ comfort also abounds” (2 Corinthians 1:5), let us welcome the sufferings of Christ with the greatest eagerness, and let them abound in us, if we really long for abundant comfort, the comfort with which all who “mourn” “will be comforted” (Matthew 5:4), though perhaps not equally. For if the comfort were equal, it would not have been written, “As the sufferings of Christ abound towards us, so our comfort also abounds.” Those who share in the sufferings will share in the comfort too, in proportion to the sufferings they share with Christ. You learn this also from the one who speaks of such things as a man entrusted with them: “For we know that as you share in the sufferings, so also in the comfort” (2 Corinthians 1:7). And God says through the prophet, “At an acceptable time I heard you, and on a day of salvation I helped you” (Isaiah 49:8). What other time, then, is so acceptable as when, for our godliness towards God in Christ, we are led away under guard, paraded through the world, triumphing rather than being led in triumph? For the martyrs in Christ strip off with him “the principalities and the powers” (Colossians 2:15) and share his triumph: as they come to share in his sufferings, so they share also in the valiant deeds done in his sufferings. Among these is the triumph over “the principalities and the powers”, which in a little while you will see conquered and put to shame. What other day is so truly a day of salvation as the day of such a release of ours from this place?

But I urge you: “give no offence in anything”, so that the presbyterate or “the ministry” “may not be discredited” through you, “but in everything commend yourselves as ministers of God, in much endurance” (2 Corinthians 6:3-4), saying, “And now what is my endurance? Is it not the Lord?” (Psalm 39:7); “in afflictions”, persuaded that “many are the afflictions of the righteous” (Psalm 34:19); “in necessities”, so that we may claim blessedness as our necessity; “in straits”, so that, travelling the strait and hard-pressed way without leaving any of it untrodden, we may come through to life (Matthew 7:14). If need be, let us commend ourselves also “in beatings, in prisons, in riots, in labours, in sleepless nights, in fastings” (2 Corinthians 6:5). For see, the Lord, and “his reward” in his hand, “to repay each one” as his works are (Revelation 22:12).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. 42); the old English was a digest: it skipped the argument on unequal comfort, the triumph procession, the presbyterate, the wordplay on necessities and straits and the closing reward, and attached 2 Corinthians 6:6-10, which belongs to ch. 43.
'ἐν ἀνάγκαις ... ἀναγκαίαν' kept as 'necessities ... our necessity'; 'ἐν στενοχωρίαις ... τὴν στενήν' kept as 'straits ... the strait way'.
'00V' read as 'οὖν'; 'ὄφψεσθε' as 'ὄψεσθε'; 'undeulav' as 'μηδεμίαν'; 'ὅτε, πολλαὶ' as 'ὅτι'; 'iv ὡς' as 'ἵν᾽ ὡς'; 'ἡ nv' as 'ἦν'.
'as a man entrusted with them': the adverb marks the speaker as one entrusted with such teaching.
